## 固定收益開篇論點

8月4日美國固定收益市場收盤延續週一由油價帶動的漲勢，近期通膨定價下修因而更具說服力，但較長期的實質利率與供給溢價並未鬆動。2年期美債殖利率下降5個基點至4.20%，5年期與10年期均下降7個基點，分別收在4.33%與4.63%；30年期下降5個基點至5.18%。上週五賣壓在週一收盤僅部分扭轉後，市場已連續兩天全面反彈，其中以中段券種最強。能源壓力減輕、Fed升息定價轉趨溫和，壓過國內需求、政策公信力與未來附息債供給等尚未消退的風險。

催化因素也從週一籠統的外交樂觀，推進到較具體的安排。伊朗正考慮允許歐洲國家協助清除荷姆茲海峽水雷，卡達表示已有提案在各方間傳閱，美國官員則稱協議可能即將達成。若能落實，航運與保險市場便可透過第三方取得航道安全保證。WTI下跌6.41%至$75.19，布蘭特原油下跌5.96%至$78.78，不僅擴大前一交易日跌幅，兩項指標也雙雙跌破週一舒緩行情的參考水準。自衝突爆發以來，能源通膨衝擊屢次推高Fed利率預期與美債殖利率；油價續跌則削弱了這股壓力。

通膨連結市場顯示，這波債市漲勢已不再幾乎全由實質殖利率驅動。10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.40%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降4個基點至2.23%。週一名目殖利率下降5個基點時，損益兩平通膨率僅收窄1個基點；週二則有更多跌幅來自預期通膨路徑下移。短期利率期貨仍反映9月約升息15個基點，並完整定價年底前升息1次，但已少於上週的2次。油價回落降低市場預期的政策緊縮負擔，卻未完全排除升息。

限制仍相當明顯。30年期殖利率雖收在5.18%，過去1週仍上升9個基點，過去1個月更上升20個基點；10年期過去1週上升2個基點，過去1個月上升14個基點。費城聯準銀行總裁Anna Paulson認為政策略具限制性，但估計基礎通膨仍介於2.4%至2.8%；一旦通膨改善停滯，Fed仍有明確理由恢復緊縮。美國財政部季度再融資說明也尚未公布，交易商正討論指引是否會開始讓市場為明年擴大固定利率借款做準備。

信用市場證實流動性運作正常，也揭露比整體漲勢更鮮明的品質分化。AbbVie發行$100億投資等級債，尖峰需求約$630億，最長天期券的最終定價較初步討論收窄33個基點。槓桿融資方面，投資人要求更寬利差後，Baker Tilly放棄約$30億貸款案，原擬搭配的再融資與最高$10億股利也未能成行。這不只是投資等級與高收益債之別：市場有充足能力承接用途清楚的併購融資，但若槓桿與再融資條件不足以補償貸方，便不願為贊助方取回資金買單。

全球傳導仍然分歧。投資人質疑美國政策公信力及日本市場穩定性，使歐洲存續期間資產獲得青睞，但歐洲本身仍有能源與財政風險。10年期JGB標售需求疲弱，加上美國收盤後公布的日本薪資數據強勁，使BOJ的升息路徑維持有效。新興市場債受惠於美國殖利率下降，卻未獲得明顯的美元流動性助力；馬達加斯加逾1年來首次升息，則顯示累積的能源成本轉嫁仍迫使當地採取政策行動。因此，週二是一波更深入的通膨降溫行情，而不是全球通膨或再融資風險同步消除。

## UST利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

美債各天期普遍上漲，但5年至10年期表現最強，這些天期的殖利率下降7個基點，超過2年期與30年期各自下降的5個基點。2s10s殖利率曲線趨平2個基點至43個基點，2s30s則維持在98個基點。曲線溫和牛市趨平，並未重演Fed會議後的扭轉式陡峭化；當時前端上漲，長端殖利率卻反而走高。週二的曲線形態顯示，市場下修中期通膨與政策負擔，但長端要求的額外補償並未消失。

週線與月線走勢仍保留這項差異。2年期殖利率過去1週下降6個基點，10年期卻上升2個基點，30年期上升9個基點；過去1個月，各天期升幅從2年期的6個基點一路擴大至30年期的20個基點。因此，單日債市上漲仍可與較長期偏緊的利率環境並存。近期升息預期雖已下修，但天期愈長，市場愈重視通膨公信力、財政融資與承擔存續期間所需的報酬。

油價最能清楚解釋通膨補償的變化。市場對荷姆茲安排的期待，已從籠統盼望展開談判，推進至可能由歐洲參與的除雷機制。不過，海峽中央航道仍需安全保證、持久停火，以及伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊同意，治理與收費方式也仍有爭議。因此，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降4個基點，是對近期能源尾端風險重新定價，並不代表市場認為實體與政治障礙已經解決。

實質殖利率也同步下降，顯示原油下跌影響的不只是整體通膨。能源衝擊減弱，可降低Fed必須抵銷第二輪效應的機率，也降低政策長時間維持限制性的風險。然而，10年期實質殖利率仍收在2.40%，只比1週前低1個基點，且比1個月前高14個基點。長天期實質殖利率同樣居高不下：30年期實質殖利率為2.96%，當日下降3個基點，過去1個月仍上升17個基點。長期投資與政府借款面對的實質報酬門檻依舊偏高。

Fed定價反映預期政策回應減弱，而非轉向降息。9月仍隱含約15個基點升息，年底前則完整定價1次25個基點升息。相較上週完整定價2次升息，這項變化相當重要，因為利率路徑已直接連結到外部通膨衝擊的緩解程度。不過，下修幅度未必穩固。7月就業報告尚待公布；週二出爐的6月職缺數降幅大於預期，市場反應卻有限，國內勞動需求在同一交易日仍沒有決定性的新訊號。

Paulson的政策框架說明市場為何仍保留部分升息定價。她認為有兩種合理情境：若基礎通膨持續改善，目前政策可能已略具足夠限制性；另一種可能是，過去1年進展有限，代表限制程度仍不足。她估計基礎通膨介於2.4%至2.8%，仍高於2%目標。6月PCE物價下降0.1%，實質消費卻成長0.4%。目前油價下跌支持較溫和的情境，但仍無法斷定國內服務與支出是否足以完成通膨降溫進程。

殖利率曲線還包含政策公信力溢價，不會因單次能源價格走勢而消失。市場對Fed主席Kevin Warsh反應函數及Fed容忍通膨程度的疑慮，曾在上次會議後推動異常的扭轉式陡峭化。週二扭轉了部分殖利率水準變化，卻未推翻背後邏輯。9月升息溢價下降，可壓低2年至10年期殖利率；但若通膨長期高於目標，或政策反應規則不透明，較長天期仍需額外補償。2s30s斜率維持98個基點不變，長債殖利率月升幅仍大，兩者都延續這種不對稱。

財政供給是判斷漲勢能否持久的另一項限制。交易商預期美國財政部在8月至10月當季維持名目附息債與浮動利率票據規模不變，但對首次增額時點的看法介於2027年2月至8月。部分交易商主張，應從承諾未來數季維持規模不變的既有指引中刪除「至少」，藉此弱化承諾。公告只能確立借款時程並釋放訊號，不能代表實際標售需求。在結果出爐前，油價下跌雖可壓低殖利率中的通膨成分，潛在融資需求仍會支撐期限溢價。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

美債上漲、風險偏好增強，帶動信用債價格普遍走高。LQD上漲0.61%，HYG上漲0.30%，JNK上漲0.31%。中長天期美債殖利率下降之際，存續期間敏感度較高的LQD漲幅也較大。基金報酬營造有利的總報酬環境，但更具判讀價值的信用訊號來自初級市場條件。規模龐大、資金用途清楚的投資等級債在強勁需求下順利去化；結合再融資與贊助方分配款的槓桿交易，卻無法達到市場可接受的價格。

AbbVie交出最強的市場承接結果。公司分9個天期發行合計$100億債券，涵蓋2年至40年期，用以協助融資尚待完成、價值$109億的Apogee Therapeutics收購案。尖峰訂單約$630億，高於AbbVie今年2月發行$80億債券時吸引的約$390億，也略高於Amazon上月$250億發行案的需求。AbbVie最長天期券以美債加碼92個基點定價，較初步討論收窄33個基點。6家投資等級發行人合計籌資$173億，顯示債市漲勢足以支撐可觀的新券供給。

需求組成與規模同樣重要。AbbVie是今年少數與AI借款潮無關的巨額交易之一，收購標的與其成熟製藥產品組合相連。近期AI與資料中心融資案，要求投資人更仔細檢視合約年限、資產汰舊風險、客戶集中度與未來供給。企業債投資組合正面對大量科技業待發供給，AbbVie因而帶來產業分散效果。這本訂單簿證明投資等級市場仍有承接能力，卻不代表所有發行人或資金用途都能獲得同樣需求。

Baker Tilly則劃出另一端的界線。這家會計師事務所取消約$30億槓桿貸款案，原擬用來再融資私募信貸債務並發放股利。部分潛在買方要求的利差，超出借款人願意接受的水準。股利最高可能達$10億，若成行將是今年非投資等級市場規模最大的一筆。交易屬機會型融資，並非為近期到期債務解圍，因此公司仍有等待空間。即便如此，交易失敗仍說明，美債上漲不代表市場願意以任何利差為贊助方取回資金。

這種差異延續近期軟體業與併購融資中由貸方主導的條件重設。借款人若願意提高讓利、強化債權文件或限制資金流向股東，仍可維持市場准入；Baker Tilly並未跨過這道門檻。透過聯貸市場再融資直接貸款機構債務，本可降低借款成本，但政策利率偏高、垃圾債到期潮逼近，買方原已占優勢，額外加入大額分配款更削弱交易吸引力。這是定價與結構問題，不代表槓桿貸款資本出現系統性短缺。

次級市場的投資等級風險也加速分化。美元與歐元投資等級債指數中，約$1,000億債券的交易利差寬於雙B級曲線，Oracle與Stellantis均是較受矚目的潛在墮落天使。Oracle的資料中心支出使疑慮集中在AI的資本密集度；Stellantis面對的則是競爭與營運表現壓力。共同傳導管道是資本成本上升與槓桿交互作用，而非單一產業衝擊。一旦遭到降評，僅能投資投資等級債的帳戶將被迫賣出，轉由規模較小的高收益債買方承接。

市場定價可能領先評等變動，因此不能機械式解讀這批債券。Oracle利差7月曾突破雙B級水準，但到8月初已重新收窄至雙B級曲線內側。單憑一檔債券相對垃圾債比較基準的交易位置，無法斷定一定會遭降評；信用分析師會以更長期間評估營收、利潤率、現金流與槓桿。然而，跨越這道界線的債券規模異常龐大，仍值得重視。融資成本、戰爭影響與AI投資正在改變市場對資產負債表的預期，投資人也迅速重估過去被視為穩定的發行人。

下一筆AI融資考驗已進一步放大。Blackstone向投資人試探至少$360億債務的興趣，用於Anthropic使用Google晶片；若成案，規模將超過數月前才完成的約$350億融資。第1筆交易中，Broadcom為最大優先部位的付款提供支持。第2筆交易將檢驗：結構性支持能否反覆把晶片租賃與仍在消耗現金的AI需求，轉化為符合投資級需求的曝險；還是投資組合容量與交易對手集中度，會要求明顯不同的定價。市政基礎設施則呈現另一種長期負債。洛杉磯計畫發行$4億水務收益債，支應截至2031財政年度逾$100億的投資；一條1916年鋪設的幹管日前破裂，當地逾30%的社區主幹管線也已使用超過80年。Moody's給予Aa3評等、Fitch給予AA-；儘管客戶基礎龐大且穩定，野火訴訟仍限制信用表現。信用市場的綜合結論，是流動性充足，但市場允許的槓桿與存續期間範圍縮小。AbbVie最終利差較初始討論收窄33個基點，成功建立2年至40年的完整發行曲線；Baker Tilly規模較小的槓桿融資，卻因投資人要求更高利差而未能完成；Anthropic擬議融資考驗異常龐大的AI承接能力；洛杉磯把必要基礎設施與訴訟及資本需求連在一起；潛在fallen angel則顯示投資級市場內部也有壓力。美國公債殖利率下降，改善評價與執行條件，但資金用途、產業集中度、契約文件、法律曝險與降評遷移仍是決定因素。這個交易日沒有消除信用風險，反而讓市場可接受風險的層級更清楚。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

全球長存續期間債券並未發出一致的寬鬆訊號。部分經理人正把資金從美債、英國公債與日本公債轉向歐元區債券，理由是當地制度與政策框架較可預測。德國10年期公債殖利率高於3%，利率交換也已反映ECB積極升息，改善了進場水準，儘管投資人對央行是否會照此路徑行動仍有分歧。這股資金流對美債構成相對價值挑戰：即使美債上漲，只要外國主權債市場提供更清楚的政策規則或更具吸引力的補償，策略性需求仍可能減少。

歐洲並非毫無瑕疵的避風港。能源曝險、國防與人口老化相關財政需求，以及政治風險，在各國之間仍不均衡。義大利預算談判限制市場對長天期資產的信心；法國10年期公債殖利率則較德國高近80個基點，部分正反映這些差異。歐元區家庭行為另添一項通膨降溫機制：伊朗戰爭後支出轉弱，主要源於不確定性及延後非必要消費，而非僅因實際價格上漲。持久的荷姆茲協議可望在壓低能源通膨之際，扭轉部分支出抑制。

日本帶來更直接的競爭性殖利率管道。週二10年期JGB標售需求降至2025年5月以來最弱，原因是國內殖利率持續波動，BOJ下一步升息的可能性仍在。單次標售疲弱不足以證明日本整體承接失靈，卻會提高本地買方要求的報酬，也使美債可獲得的海外需求更加不確定。匯市干預可降低輸入性通膨，但JGB殖利率若預期走高，仍可能吸引資金回流日本。FIMA融資限制已迫使美債遭到出售，卻不會消除相對殖利率的取捨。

美國收盤後公布的日本薪資數據，進一步拉高政策張力。6月名目薪資與基本薪資均較1年前成長3.4%，較穩定的全職員工薪資指標成長2.9%，實質薪資成長1.7%，已連續6個月上升。名目薪資增幅高於3%已持續5個月，創34年來最長紀錄。數據公布時，週二美債走勢早已收盤，因此不能用來解釋當日行情；但數據確實提高BOJ未來數月再度升息的可能，也讓JGB標售疲弱對全球買方基礎更具前瞻意義。

儘管油價最新回落，亞洲整體總體經濟情勢仍帶有停滯性通膨色彩。亞洲開發銀行把開發中亞洲及太平洋地區的2026年成長預測從5.1%下修至4.9%，並把通膨預測從3.6%上調至4.3%。能源進口經濟體先前已出現生產受限與家庭需求轉弱，現貨油價下降無法立即扭轉這些影響。成長下修、通膨上修也意味政策將持續分歧：部分央行可以等待成本轉嫁消退，外部條件較弱的經濟體仍須捍衛通膨預期與金融穩定。

印度國內流動性也在推動一輪離岸融資。銀行今年已取得$127億境外貸款，預計2026年剩餘期間還可籌得最高$300億，使全年規模接近創紀錄的$430億。銀行與國營融資機構也可能在已發行$108億全球債券之外，再籌最高$100億。背後驅動力是銀行競相吸收非居民印度人的外幣存款，利率超過7%；部分銀行獲准提供最高為原始存款19倍的貸款。這項結構擴大美元融資與金融中介能力，但也在看似單純的存款流入背後，引入槓桿與續作敏感度。馬達加斯加則採取相反的本地政策回應。該國央行把政策利率從12%調升至12.5%，是逾1年來首次升息，此前並已把年底通膨預測從9.3%上調至10.1%。決策者認為第2季貨幣環境的限制性不足，並維持5%的中期通膨目標。央行升息時，和平希望正把油價推近$80，凸顯全球商品價格反轉傳導到國內政策舒緩存在時滯。對美債而言，海外淨影響仍然分歧：歐洲提供相對價值替代選項；印度把前端流動性與擴大的美元金融中介結合；日本提高本地殖利率門檻；依賴進口的經濟體則面臨延後的緊縮週期。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

新興市場債跟隨長存續期間債券上漲，卻未獲得全面的美元流動性助力。EMB上漲0.50%，15年以上新興市場美元主權債指數上漲0.66%，美元指數則僅下跌0.09%至99.873。長天期主權債指數漲幅較大，符合美國殖利率下降帶來的舒緩效果；但該指數過去1週下跌0.46%，過去1個月下跌2.90%，顯示共同的長存續期間負擔依舊存在。因此，單日指數上漲應解讀為總報酬回升，而非主權債現券利差全面收窄。

原油下跌最直接扭轉能源進口國面對的共同衝擊，但區域成長與通膨預測調整也說明，舒緩程度不會一致。家庭與企業已承受燃料費用上升、生產中斷與需求轉弱；部分主權國家還面對補貼或支持措施帶來的第二輪財政成本。馬達加斯加等央行依據通膨預測採取行動，而非追隨最新結算價。荷姆茲若能持續恢復通行，後續路徑將會改善；但原油再跌一天，仍無法修復受損的資產負債表或政策空間。

中國實力較弱的地方借款人仍有獨立的債務管理風險，但目前沒有新資訊改變洛陽商都先前已確立的到期事實，因此不必再次鋪陳其延後境外再融資與聲稱以現金償還的計畫。更廣泛的意涵仍可從當前市場排序看出：基準存續期間資產可以上漲，邊際發行人卻仍缺乏以可接受條件成交的證明。主權、準主權與企業的融資准入必須分開判斷，因為具有官方關係，不代表有爭議的再融資就能轉化為主權流動性。

Zimbabwe增加的是主權債務重整管道，而非市場價格訊號。France與UK將共同領導債務諮詢小組，首次會議將處理估計達$213億的公共債務。建立債權人論壇本身不會降低債務存量，也不能證明已就處理條件達成共識；但它提供協調官方債權人、欠款與未來市場准入所需的制度架構。新興市場的結論是：市場透過美國折現率下降獲得紓壓，而非美元全面寬鬆。長天期硬通貨債券上漲，美元則幾乎持平，本地政策仍反映先前累積的能源損害。這種組合有利於依能源進口程度、外匯存底深度、財政支援能力、債權人協調與到期結構區分市場，也意味即使最強的共同因子在週二轉為有利，新興市場仍容易受到油價外交逆轉或美國實質殖利率再度上升的衝擊。

## 跨資產

跨資產走勢支持通膨與地緣政治風險舒緩的解讀，而非成長恐慌。標普500指數上漲1.79%並創收盤新高，Nasdaq 100上漲3.32%，半導體指數大漲6.55%。油價大幅下跌之際，股市與美債同步上漲，符合能源成本負擔下降、預期政策回應減弱的情境。漲勢集中於科技股，也顯示折現率下降放大長存續期間股票的表現。企業獲利穩健同樣推升股市，因此不能把漲勢全歸因於油價。

風險指標並未一致傳遞平靜訊號。儘管股市上漲，VIX仍上升4.04%至16.50，黃金也上漲2.33%至$4,127.80。股市創新高、原油下跌、美債殖利率下降之際，金價仍同步上漲，顯示市場繼續防範外交進展逆轉與政策不確定性。美元僅下跌0.09%，幅度不足以解釋整體風險資產或新興市場債的漲勢。眼前環境雖然改善，避險需求仍清晰可見。

投資等級與高收益債基金雙雙上漲，完成當日有利的跨資產組合；兩者相對漲幅也更符合存續期間壓力舒緩，而非風險溢價無差別崩跌。因此，綜合訊號比全面風險偏好行情更為狹窄：油價下跌重塑通膨路徑，股市受惠於折現率下降，債券總報酬也改善。然而，波動率與金價走高，加上槓桿融資失敗、長端殖利率月線仍升，使這個交易日仍不足以代表信心全面恢復。

## 前瞻市場意義

荷姆茲進程必須把外交措辭化為持久的實體通行，週二的通膨重新定價才會成為結構性變化。歐洲參與除雷、伊朗提供安全保證、伊斯蘭革命衛隊同意及停火持續，都是必要條件；航運與保險恢復正常，則是能源供給恢復傳導到市場的可觀察證據。若原油持續下跌，損益兩平通膨率與實質殖利率同步下降，當前漲勢將沿著通膨與政策兩條管道延續。若航道治理、收費或海上安全談判破局並推高油價，最重要的新變數便會逆轉，壓力將先回到Fed定價與5年至10年期美債。

週五公布的7月就業報告，將區分外部通膨降溫與國內政策路徑。若勞動市場數據強勁，尤其薪資敏感指標與失業率顯示經濟資源壓力持續，將支持Paulson較不溫和的情境，也就是略具限制性的政策仍未帶來足夠進展。即使油價仍低於週一水準，最直接的市場反應也會是重新建立9月升息定價，2年期與5年期券種再度走弱。若勞動情勢轉弱，只有在實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步下降時，才足以深化環境轉變；若漲勢只來自通膨補償下降，偏高的實質報酬門檻與不確定的反應函數仍會存在。

8月5日季度再融資公告，將決定剩餘長端溢價有多少來自近期供給訊號。若重申名目附息債與浮動利率票據規模「至少」數季維持不變，可延後眼前的存續期間衝擊；若刪除「至少」，或以其他方式讓投資人為2027年2月增額做準備，承接問題將提前浮現。後續標售尾差或標售結果優於發行前水準、投標倍數與配售比重，只有在實際標售時相對各自參考值判讀才有意義。指引穩定且需求有序，可讓油價下跌主導10年至30年期曲線；若提早釋出供給訊號，即使Fed路徑繼續轉趨溫和，長端溢價仍會延續。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 4 U.S. fixed-income close extended Monday's oil-led rally and made the near-term inflation repricing more convincing, without dislodging the longer-run real-rate and supply premium. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 5 basis points to 4.20%, the 5- and 10-year yields each declined 7 basis points to 4.33% and 4.63%, and the 30-year fell 5 basis points to 5.18%. The current change is a second day of broad relief after the prior close's partial reversal of Friday's selloff. Its hierarchy was clearest in the belly, where reduced energy pressure and less aggressive Fed pricing outweighed the still-live risks from domestic demand, policy credibility and future coupon supply.

The catalyst also advanced beyond Monday's general diplomatic optimism. Iran was considering allowing European countries to help remove mines from the Strait of Hormuz, Qatar said a proposal had been circulated, and U.S. officials indicated an agreement could be imminent. That prospect offered shipping and insurance markets a route toward third-party assurance that the waterway is safe. WTI fell 6.41% to $75.19 and Brent dropped 5.96% to $78.78, deepening the previous session's declines and carrying both benchmarks below the levels that had framed Monday's relief. The move reduced an inflation shock that had repeatedly pulled Fed expectations and Treasury yields higher since the conflict began.

Inflation-linked pricing shows that the rally was no longer almost entirely a real-yield event. The 10-year real yield declined 3 basis points to 2.40%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 4 basis points to 2.23%. Monday's 5-basis-point nominal rally had included only 1 basis point of breakeven compression; Tuesday's move assigned more of the change to a lower expected inflation path. Short-rate futures also priced about 15 basis points of tightening for September and one full increase by year-end, down from two increases as recently as last week. Oil relief altered the expected policy burden, even though it did not eliminate tightening.

The limits remain substantial. At 5.18%, the 30-year yield was still 9 basis points higher over 1 week and 20 basis points higher over 1 month. The 10-year was 2 basis points higher over the week and 14 basis points higher over the month. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson described policy as mildly restrictive but estimated underlying inflation at 2.4% to 2.8%, leaving a clear route to renewed restraint if progress stalls. Treasury's quarterly refunding communication was still ahead, with dealers debating whether guidance would begin preparing the market for larger fixed-rate borrowing programs next year.

Credit confirmed functioning liquidity but exposed a sharper quality divide than the broad rally implied. AbbVie's $10 billion investment-grade sale drew about $63 billion of peak demand, and its longest maturity priced 33 basis points tighter than initial discussion. In leveraged finance, Baker Tilly abandoned a roughly $3 billion loan after investors sought wider spreads, blocking a refinancing that also contemplated a dividend of as much as $1 billion. The contrast is not simply investment grade against high yield. It shows strong capacity for identifiable acquisition financing and weak tolerance for sponsor extraction when leverage and refinancing economics do not compensate lenders.

Global transmission remained mixed. European duration attracted interest as investors questioned U.S. policy credibility and Japanese market stability, yet Europe still carried energy and fiscal risks. A weak 10-year JGB auction and, after the U.S. close, firm Japanese wage data kept the BOJ tightening path active. Emerging-market debt benefited from lower U.S. yields without a meaningful dollar-liquidity impulse, while Madagascar's first rate increase in more than a year showed that accumulated energy pass-through was still forcing local policy action. Tuesday was therefore a deeper disinflation rally, not a synchronized removal of global inflation or refinancing risk.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The Treasury move was broad but strongest from 5 to 10 years. The 7-basis-point declines in those maturities exceeded the 5-basis-point falls at both the 2-year and 30-year points. The 2s10s curve flattened 2 basis points to 43, while 2s30s remained at 98. This was a modest bull flattening rather than a return to the post-Fed twist steepening that had pushed long yields higher as the front end rallied. The daily shape says the market reduced the expected inflation and policy burden across the intermediate horizon, but did not remove the distinct compensation still demanded at the long end.

The weekly and monthly profiles preserve that distinction. The 2-year yield was 6 basis points lower over 1 week, whereas the 10-year was 2 basis points higher and the 30-year 9 basis points higher. Over 1 month, the increases ranged from 6 basis points at 2 years to 20 basis points at 30 years. The daily rally can therefore coexist with a more restrictive longer-horizon regime. Near-term tightening has been marked down, but inflation credibility, fiscal financing and the required return on duration continue to rise in importance with maturity.

Oil supplied the cleanest explanation for the change in inflation compensation. The prospective Hormuz arrangement moved from a broad hope for talks toward a possible demining mechanism, with European participation under discussion. A central channel through the strait would still require security assurances, a durable ceasefire and agreement from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Governance and fee collection also remain disputed. The 4-basis-point decline in the 10-year breakeven is consequently a repricing of the immediate energy tail, not a market judgment that the physical and political obstacles have been resolved.

Real yields also fell, indicating that lower crude affected more than headline inflation. A diminished energy shock reduces the likelihood that the Fed must offset second-round effects and lowers the risk that policy remains restrictive for longer. The 10-year real yield nevertheless closed at 2.40%, only 1 basis point below its level a week earlier and 14 basis points above its month-earlier level. Long real yields showed a similar persistence: the 30-year real yield was 2.96%, down 3 basis points on the day but still 17 basis points higher over 1 month. The real hurdle for long-lived investment and public borrowing remains high.

Fed pricing reflected a smaller expected response rather than a pivot to easing. About 15 basis points of tightening remained embedded for September, and one 25-basis-point increase was fully priced by year-end. The change from two fully priced increases last week is material because it links the rate path directly to relief in an externally generated inflation impulse. It is also fragile. The July employment report remains ahead, and Tuesday's larger-than-expected decline in June job openings produced little market reaction, leaving domestic labor demand without a decisive same-session update.

Paulson's policy framework explains why the market retained some tightening. She sees two plausible states: current policy may be mildly restrictive enough if underlying inflation continues to improve, or the limited progress over the past year may indicate that it is not restrictive enough. Her estimate of underlying inflation between 2.4% and 2.8% remains above the 2% objective. June PCE prices fell 0.1%, but real consumption rose 0.4%. The current oil decline supports the benign branch; it does not settle whether domestic services and spending will complete the disinflation process.

The curve also carries a policy-credibility premium that one energy move cannot erase. Questions about Chairman Kevin Warsh's reaction function and the Fed's tolerance for inflation had driven an unusual twist steepening after the previous meeting. Tuesday reversed some of its level effect, not its logic. A smaller September premium can lower 2- to 10-year yields, yet a prolonged period of inflation above target or an opaque response rule still requires compensation farther out. The unchanged 98-basis-point 2s30s slope and the long bond's large monthly rise preserve that asymmetry.

Fiscal supply is the second constraint on calling the rally durable. Dealers expected Treasury to maintain nominal coupon and floating-rate note sizes for the August-to-October quarter, but views on the first increase ranged from February to August 2027. Some favored softening the standing guidance by removing the phrase "at least" from a commitment to steady sizes for several quarters. The announcement would establish the borrowing calendar and signal, not auction demand. Until actual results arrive, lower oil can reduce the inflation component of yields while prospective financing needs continue to support term premium.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit prices improved with the Treasury rally and stronger risk appetite. LQD gained 0.61%, HYG rose 0.30% and JNK added 0.31%. The larger move in LQD is consistent with its greater duration sensitivity on a day when intermediate and long Treasury yields fell. These returns establish a favorable total-return backdrop, but the more informative credit evidence came from primary-market terms. Large, strategically legible investment-grade supply cleared with exceptional demand, while a leveraged transaction combining refinancing and sponsor distribution failed to reach an acceptable price.

AbbVie provided the strongest absorption result. The company sold $10 billion across nine maturities from 2 to 40 years to help finance its pending $10.9 billion acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics. Peak orders reached about $63 billion, above the roughly $39 billion drawn by AbbVie's $8 billion February sale and slightly above demand for Amazon's $25 billion offering last month. The longest AbbVie tranche priced at 92 basis points over Treasuries, 33 basis points tighter than initial discussion. Six investment-grade issuers raised a combined $17.3 billion, showing that the rally could support a substantial new-issue calendar.

The composition of demand is as important as its size. AbbVie's deal was one of the few jumbo transactions this year unrelated to the AI borrowing wave, and it financed an acquisition tied to an established pharmaceutical portfolio. Recent AI and data-center financings had required greater scrutiny of contract life, asset obsolescence, customer concentration and future supply. AbbVie offered sector diversification at a moment when corporate portfolios were confronting a heavy technology pipeline. The orderbook therefore demonstrates available investment-grade capacity, but not uniform demand for every issuer or use of proceeds.

Baker Tilly marked the opposite boundary. The accounting firm dropped a roughly $3 billion leveraged loan intended to refinance private credit debt and fund a dividend. Some prospective buyers required wider spreads than the borrower was prepared to offer. The dividend could have reached $1 billion and would have been the year's largest in non-investment-grade markets. The proposed transaction was opportunistic rather than a near-term maturity rescue, giving the company room to wait. Its failure still shows that a Treasury rally does not make sponsor extraction financeable at any spread.

This distinction extends the lender-led reset visible in recent software and acquisition financings. Borrowers can preserve access by paying a larger concession, strengthening documentation or limiting value leakage. Baker Tilly did not cross that threshold. Refinancing direct-lender debt through the syndicated market might have reduced borrowing costs, but adding a large distribution weakened the proposition when high policy rates and looming junk maturities already favored buyers. The failed deal is a pricing and structure event, not evidence of a systemwide shortage of leveraged-loan capital.

Secondary investment-grade risk also became more explicitly segmented. About $100 billion of bonds in U.S. dollar and euro investment-grade indexes had traded at spreads wider than the double-B curve, placing Oracle and Stellantis among prominent potential fallen angels. Oracle's data-center spending concentrates the concern in AI capital intensity; Stellantis faces a different pressure from competition and operating performance. The common channel is a higher cost of capital interacting with leverage, not a single sector shock. A downgrade would also force selling by investment-grade-only mandates into a smaller high-yield buyer base.

Market pricing can move ahead of ratings, which limits a mechanical reading of that cohort. Oracle's spreads had already moved back inside double-B levels by the start of August after breaching them in July. A bond trading through a junk comparison does not ensure a downgrade, and credit analysts assess revenue, margins, cash flow and leverage over a longer horizon. The unusually large volume crossing that boundary still matters because it shows how quickly investors are repricing formerly stable issuers when funding costs, war effects and AI investment alter balance-sheet expectations.

The next AI financing test was already becoming larger. Blackstone had sounded out investors on at least $36 billion of debt to finance Anthropic's use of Google chips, which would exceed the approximately $35 billion package completed only months earlier. Broadcom had backstopped payments on the largest senior portions of the first transaction. A second deal would test whether structural support can repeatedly convert chip leases and cash-burning AI demand into investment-grade-compatible exposure, or whether portfolio capacity and counterparty concentration require materially different pricing. Municipal infrastructure presented a different long-lived liability. Los Angeles planned to sell $400 million of water-revenue bonds toward more than $10 billion of spending through fiscal 2031 after a 1916 trunk line ruptured; more than 30% of its neighborhood mainlines were over 80 years old. Moody's rated the bonds Aa3 and Fitch AA-, with wildfire litigation constraining the credit despite a stable and exceptionally large customer base. The combined credit conclusion is ample liquidity with narrower permission for leverage and duration. AbbVie compressed 33 basis points from initial discussion and filled a 2- to 40-year curve; Baker Tilly could not complete a smaller leveraged package when investors demanded more spread; the proposed Anthropic financing tested exceptional AI capacity; Los Angeles linked essential infrastructure to litigation and capital needs; and potential fallen angels revealed pressure inside the investment-grade universe itself. Lower Treasury yields improved marks and execution conditions, but use of proceeds, sector concentration, documentation, legal exposure and downgrade migration remained decisive. The session did not remove credit risk; it made the market's hierarchy of acceptable risk easier to observe.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Global duration did not produce a single easing signal. Some managers were reallocating from Treasuries, gilts and Japanese bonds toward euro-area debt, citing a more predictable institutional and policy framework. German 10-year yields above 3% and aggressive ECB tightening priced into swaps had improved entry levels, even as investors differed on whether the central bank would deliver that path. The flow argument is a relative-value challenge for Treasuries: a U.S. rally can coexist with reduced strategic demand if foreign sovereign markets offer clearer policy rules or more attractive compensation.

Europe is not a clean haven. Energy exposure, defense and ageing-related fiscal needs, and political risks remain uneven across countries. Italian budget negotiations constrain long-duration confidence, while French 10-year debt offered nearly 80 basis points over Germany partly because of those differences. Euro-area household behavior adds a disinflationary mechanism: spending weakened after the Iran war mainly through uncertainty and delayed discretionary consumption, rather than only through realized price increases. A durable Hormuz agreement could reverse some of that restraint even as it lowers energy inflation.

Japan supplied a more immediate competitive yield channel. Tuesday's 10-year JGB auction drew its weakest demand since May 2025, as domestic yields remained volatile and the next BOJ move stayed live. A weak auction does not establish a broad failure of Japanese absorption, but it raises the return required by local buyers and complicates the foreign demand available for Treasuries. Yen intervention can reduce imported inflation, yet higher prospective JGB yields can still draw capital home. FIMA funding limits forced Treasury sales, but it does not eliminate the relative-yield decision.

After the U.S. close, Japanese wage data strengthened that policy tension. Nominal and base pay both rose 3.4% from a year earlier in June, the stable full-time measure increased 2.9%, and real wages gained 1.7% for a sixth consecutive month. Nominal gains above 3% have now lasted five months, the longest run in 34 years. The release cannot explain Tuesday's completed Treasury move. It does reinforce the prospect of another BOJ increase in coming months and gives the weak JGB auction greater forward significance for the global buyer base.

Asia's broader macro picture remains stagflationary despite the latest oil decline. The Asian Development Bank lowered its 2026 growth forecast for developing Asia and the Pacific to 4.9% from 5.1% and raised its inflation projection to 4.3% from 3.6%. Energy-importing economies had already experienced curtailed production and weaker household demand, creating effects that a lower spot oil price cannot immediately reverse. The combination argues for policy dispersion: some central banks can wait for pass-through to fade, while weaker external positions must still defend inflation expectations and financial stability.

India's domestic liquidity was also feeding an offshore funding cycle. Banks were expected to raise as much as $30 billion of offshore loans during the rest of 2026 after securing $12.7 billion, potentially taking the annual total near a record $43 billion. Banks and state-owned financiers could add as much as $10 billion of global bonds on top of $10.8 billion already raised. The driver was competition for nonresident Indian foreign-currency deposits paying above 7%, with some banks permitted to lend as much as 19 times the original deposit. That structure broadens dollar funding and intermediation, but introduces leverage and rollover sensitivity behind the apparent deposit inflow. Madagascar showed the opposite local-policy response. Its central bank raised the policy rate to 12.5% from 12%, the first increase in more than a year, after lifting its year-end inflation forecast to 10.1% from 9.3%. Policymakers judged second-quarter monetary conditions insufficiently restrictive and retained a 5% medium-term inflation target. The action occurred as oil approached $80 on peace hopes, illustrating the lag between a global commodity reversal and domestic policy relief. For Treasuries, the net foreign impulse remains mixed: Europe offers a relative-value alternative, India combines front-end liquidity with expanding dollar intermediation, Japan presents a rising local yield hurdle, and import-dependent economies retain delayed tightening cycles.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt participated in the duration rally without a broad dollar-liquidity tailwind. EMB gained 0.50%, and the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign bond index rose 0.66%. The Dollar Index slipped only 0.09% to 99.873. The stronger move in the long sovereign index fits relief from lower U.S. yields, but its 0.46% loss over 1 week and 2.90% decline over 1 month show that the common long-duration burden remains. Daily index gains should therefore be read as total-return recovery, not as a uniform tightening in sovereign cash spreads.

Lower crude changes the direction of the common shock most directly for energy importers, yet the regional growth and inflation revisions show why relief will be uneven. Households and firms have already absorbed higher fuel bills, production interruptions and weaker demand. Some sovereigns face the second-round fiscal cost of subsidies or support measures, while central banks such as Madagascar's are responding to inflation forecasts rather than the latest settlement price. A sustained reopening of Hormuz would improve the path; one more decline in crude cannot restore damaged balance sheets or policy space.

China's weaker local borrowers remain a separate debt-management risk, but the current window did not change the previously established maturity facts for Luoyang Shangdu. Its delayed offshore refinancing and stated cash repayment plan therefore do not warrant a renewed narrative. The broader implication remains visible through the current market hierarchy: benchmark duration can rally while marginal issuers still lack transaction proof at acceptable terms. Sovereign, quasi-sovereign and corporate access must be distinguished because official association does not convert a contested refinancing into sovereign liquidity.

Zimbabwe added a sovereign-restructuring channel rather than a market-price signal. France and the UK were set to lead a Debt Consultative Group whose first meeting would address public debt estimated at $21.3 billion. Establishing the creditor forum does not itself reduce the stock or prove agreed treatment, but it creates the coordination structure needed to reconcile official creditors, arrears and future access. The EM conclusion is relief through the U.S. discount rate rather than a generalized dollar easing. Long hard-currency duration gained, the dollar was almost unchanged, and local policy continued to reflect accumulated energy damage. That combination favors dispersion by import dependence, reserve depth, fiscal support capacity, creditor coordination and maturity structure. It also leaves EM exposed to a reversal in oil diplomacy or a renewed rise in U.S. real yields, even after the strongest common factor moved in a supportive direction on Tuesday.

## Cross asset

Cross assets support an inflation and geopolitical relief interpretation rather than a growth scare. The S&P 500 gained 1.79% to a record close, the Nasdaq 100 rose 3.32% and the semiconductor index surged 6.55%. Stocks and Treasuries rising together as oil fell sharply is consistent with a lower energy tax and a smaller expected policy response. The concentration in technology also indicates that falling discount rates amplified the move in long-duration equities. Solid corporate earnings contributed, so the equity rally cannot be assigned to oil alone.

Risk measures did not deliver a uniformly calm message. The VIX rose 4.04% to 16.50 despite the equity advance, and gold gained 2.33% to $4,127.80. Gold's rise alongside record equities, lower crude and falling Treasury yields indicates continued demand for protection against a diplomatic reversal or policy uncertainty. The dollar's 0.09% decline was too small to explain the broad risk rally or the EM debt gain. Immediate conditions improved, but hedging demand remained visible.

Credit funds completed the favorable same-day pattern, with both investment-grade and high-yield vehicles higher. Their relative moves were also consistent with duration relief rather than an indiscriminate collapse in risk premiums. The combined check is therefore narrower than a universal risk-on signal: oil repriced the inflation path, equities welcomed lower discount rates, and bond total returns improved. Higher volatility and gold, together with failed leveraged financing and persistent long-yield increases over the month, keep the session from qualifying as a full restoration of confidence.

## Forward Market Significance

The Hormuz process must turn diplomatic language into durable physical access before Tuesday's inflation repricing becomes structural. European demining participation, Iranian security assurances, IRGC consent and a ceasefire that holds are the conditions that matter; shipping and insurance normalization would provide the observable transmission into energy supply. Continued declines in crude accompanied by lower breakevens and real yields would extend the current rally through both inflation and policy channels. A failure over waterway governance, fee collection or naval security that sends oil back higher would reverse the most important new input and restore pressure first to Fed pricing and the 5- to 10-year Treasury sector.

Friday's July employment report separates external disinflation from the domestic policy path. A firm labor result, particularly if wage-sensitive measures and unemployment indicate continuing capacity pressure, would support Paulson's less-benign scenario in which mildly restrictive policy is not delivering enough progress. The sensitive response would be a rebuilding of September tightening and renewed weakness in the 2-year and 5-year sectors even if oil remains below Monday's levels. A softer labor picture would deepen the regime change only if real yields decline alongside breakevens; an inflation-compensation rally alone would leave the high real hurdle and uncertain reaction function intact.

The August 5 quarterly refunding announcement determines how much of the remaining long-end premium belongs to near-term supply signaling. Repeating that nominal coupon and floating-rate note sizes will remain steady for at least several quarters would defer an immediate duration shock, whereas removing "at least" or otherwise preparing investors for increases in February 2027 would bring the absorption question closer. Subsequent auction tails or throughs, bid-to-cover ratios and allocation shares will matter only against their stated references when those sales occur. Stable guidance and orderly demand could let lower oil dominate the 10- to 30-year curve; an earlier supply signal would preserve the long-end premium even if the Fed path continues to soften.
